question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

__Since setting up__, the charity has raised a million dollars.
solution:
The correct option is: **Since being set up**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, the use of 'Since being set up' is correct.
 
• This option improves the original part ("Since setting up") of the sentence by correcting its grammatical structure and maintaining the intended meaning.
 
• "Since being set up" is the appropriate phrase to use when referring to the **period** from the time the charity was established to the present.
 
• It signifies the time from the moment of creation ("being set up") until now ("since").

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Since being set up__**, the charity has raised a million dollars.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Explanation for the incorrect options:
 
 
• **From setting up: **This phrase changes the original meaning of the sentence. "From setting up" suggests that the act of setting up the charity itself generated the million dollars, which is not the same as the intended meaning (the charity has raised a million dollars since it was established).
 
• **Since setting:** This is grammatically incorrect and unclear. It suggests an ongoing action but does not specify what that action is, leaving the sentence incomplete.
 
• **No improvement required:** This option suggests that the original sentence is grammatically correct, which is not the case. The phrase "since setting up" is grammatically awkward and incomplete. It needs to be improved for proper syntax and clarity of meaning.
